self.graph is not the module's designated @graph (it's an attribute of an external object), so the query uses the explicit call suffix s{ ... }(self.graph) rather than a @graph declaration.
row.prop / row.range attribute access on the s{ } iteration result works unchanged: it stays an rdflib ResultRow.

repair.remaining: Mutants déjà tués avant : îlot vidé, OPTIONAL retiré, classe élargie, rdfs:range élargi, garde forcée à False. Équivalents : DISTINCT retiré (dict réécrit par clé), `is not None` -> truthiness (un Graph vide ne donne aucune ligne).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the query string inlined into the for; `str(row.range) if row.range else XSD_STRING` becomes str(row.range or XSD_STRING) (same on None and on a falsy literal) assigned directly; the two identical loops over entities and relations merged into one loop over both (same order). The `if key not in xsd_map` test is kept rather than setdefault, which would evaluate _PY_TO_XSD.get eagerly and raise on an unhashable type the original never looks up. DISTINCT kept (it can change which range wins on a store that repeats rows).
optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the query in s{ }(self.graph) with the two @prefix lines in the if-block; OPTIONAL keeps it out of m{ }.
header_optimization_notes: Python and LD Python alike: `from typing import Dict, List, Set, Literal, Optional` becomes `from typing import Dict`.
